identityReview: Mohammed Shia al-Sudani, born Baghdad 1970 to Maysan family; month/day not independently corroborated sufficiently, so birth field uses year only. IIER CV confirms 1992 Baghdad agriculture bachelor, not independently verified 1997 project-management master or doctorate. Agriculture service 1997, Amarah administration 2004, provincial council 2005–2009, governor 2009–2010, human rights ministry 2010–2014, labour/social affairs 2014–2018. Prime minister from October 27, 2022; successor Zaidi parliamentary oath May 14, 2026, formal handover May 16. Current coalition leader/former premier, not current Iraqi PM, Sudanese president or Kurdistan regional prime minister.
lifeStatusEvidence: KRG official report confirms October 12, 2026 meeting with Masrour Barzani; NINA reports November 2 meeting with incumbent premier Zaidi, quoting PM office. 964 Media reports actual November 12 Baghdad reception of Bafel Talabani and Shaswar Abdulwahid, quoting Sudani’s office. These are completed-event accounts rather than advance schedules; original video/photo pixels not inspected.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read Arabic historical CV and biographical narrative, contemporaneous UN/Turkish government formation statements, VOA project announcement, IPU specific election fields and Reuters final-results report, Rudaw named-spokesperson withdrawal report, Reuters parliamentary oath, Anadolu completed handover, KRG official meeting, NINA and 964 recent-event reports. Read Commons/DVIDS portrait metadata and public-domain notice; no portrait pixels.
corrections: Read four-page Arabic CV hosted by Iraqi Institute for Economic Reform: Baghdad 1970, University of Baghdad agriculture bachelor 1992, agriculture service from June 4, 1997, Amarah local administration 2004, provincial council 2005–2009, governor 2009, human rights ministry December 2010, labour ministry September 8, 2014–October 24, 2018 and acting portfolios. Use month precision for December 2010 and year precision for 2009, not false precision from contradictory secondary term tables. Current-office text in this old CV is historical, not a 2026 mandate certification.

Read Al Jazeera Arabic biography updated December 2024: Baghdad birth, family from Maysan, 1992 agriculture degree, local/provincial career, 2009 governorship, 2010–2014 human rights and 2014–2018 labour/social affairs. Distinguish acting portfolios. Its lead calls October 13, 2022 the start of premiership; contemporaneous UN and Turkish government accounts instead anchor confidence and government start on October 27. Not used as a current-role source. Founder/date accounts for Euphrates movement vary, so no precise founding date is adopted.

Read UN Iraq statement: October 27, 2022 government formation, 21 ministries filled including three women and two still vacant. Statement signed October 28 and local page dated October 29; neither publication date replaces the confidence date. Calls for reform/accountability are aspirations, not proof of achieved governance outcomes.

Read contemporaneous Turkish Foreign Ministry statement dated October 27, 2022 explicitly welcoming that day’s parliamentary confidence vote and Sudani assuming the premiership. Distinguish presidential designation earlier in October from approved government formation, and external diplomatic support from certification of domestic performance.

Read VOA May 27, 2023 full transport-project announcement: Baghdad meeting, Gulf-to-Türkiye railway/road concept, proposed $17 billion and 1200 km, further discussions required. This is a plan/estimated scale, not a completed corridor or verified diversification result. Article does not establish that later financing, procurement or all construction phases were completed.

Read IPU Parline 2025 election date, 329 total seats and coalition table entry 46. Page marks results unofficial and has inconsistent fields: 30.1% largest-party figure does not equal 46/329, turnout denominator also conflicts with electoral reporting. No turnout, percentage, other-party totals or complete-table accuracy claim adopted. Coalition seat count independently verified against Reuters quoting election commission.

Read Reuters November 17, 2025 substantive final-results report: Sudani list 46 of 329, largest individual list but coalition-building still needed. General vote November 11, initial-result photos November 12 and commission announcement November 17 are distinct. A plurality does not confer direct popular election as prime minister or guarantee another term. No full certification/complaints record audit claimed.

Read Rudaw January 12, 2026 named coalition-spokesperson account: leadership decided to withdraw Sudani’s candidacy in favour of Maliki to break Coordination Framework deadlock. This announcement did not end caretaker duties that day and did not make Maliki prime minister. Subsequent completed succession is separately documented.

Read Reuters May 14, 2026 article updated May 15: Ali al-Zaidi sworn in on Thursday, parliament approved 14 ministers with remaining portfolios unsettled. Parliamentary approval and oath differ from May 16 handover. No claim that the entire cabinet was complete or that a delayed portfolio vote prolonged Sudani’s full premiership.

Read Anadolu May 16, 2026 completed handover report citing INA, with April 27 designation and May 14 confidence context. Handover in Baghdad on May 16 establishes successor taking over duties from Sudani; do not call May 16 the earlier parliamentary oath date or adopt an unqualified single date for all stages.

Read KRG official Arabic October 12, 2026 meeting report: Masrour Barzani receives former federal prime minister and Reconstruction and Development Coalition leader. Distinguish Masrour from Masoud Barzani. KRG budget demands and cooperation positions are not enacted federal budget allocations; no outcome figures adopted.

Read NINA November 2, 2026 substantive report quoting Zaidi’s media office: actual evening meeting with Sudani as coalition leader, discussing development, reform and anti-corruption. Current navigation on November 18 is not the meeting date. Claims of intended reform are not independent proof that corruption was eliminated.

Read 964 Media November 12, 2026 completed meeting report and attributed Sudani-office statement: Bafel Talabani and Shaswar Abdulwahid visit him in Baghdad, with Haider al-Fawadi present. It supports recent personal political activity and coalition leadership, not renewed premiership, a finalized coalition agreement or enacted reforms.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No independently authenticated diploma or birth certificate, comprehensive election complaints/court file, full project-finance or construction-completion audit, current parliamentary mandate certificate, historical term-boundary legal audit or portrait pixels reviewed. IPU inconsistent fields not carried into content. Political meeting statements and development promises remain attributed proposals, not enacted outcomes.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages checked against Chinese and English: Baghdad 1970/Maysan family, 1992 agricultural bachelor only, 1997 work and 2004 Amarah versus 2005–2009 council/2009 governorship; 2010–2014 human rights and September 8, 2014–2018 labour ministry with acting portfolios distinct; October 27, 2022 government; May 27, 2023 $17 billion/1200 km planned corridor; November 11, 2025 election/November 17 results, 46 of 329 not majority or direct PM vote; January 12, 2026 candidacy withdrawal not immediate departure/Maliki accession; May 14 Zaidi confidence/oath versus May 16 handover; recent October 12 and November 2/12 meetings, correct former role and Masrour/Bafel/Shaswar identities.
